A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vector Scaffolding work. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original vectorization experiments on Kodak and DIV2K, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and qualitative demonstrations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and the main-text and appendix demonstrations.

M1.justification: The three method components, rendering formulation, losses, pruning, and optimization procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The redesigned diagrams illustrate the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain Kodak and DIV2K evaluations, the DanbooRegion qualitative example, and the 8000×8000 Earth level-of-detail demonstration. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DiffVG and Bézier Splatting as Kodak comparators. Table 2 retains DiffVG, LIVE, LIVSS, and Bézier Splatting for DIV2K. The qualitative comparisons also retain the same baselines.

E3.justification: Both use the same curve budgets, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, optimization budgets, 800-image DIV2K evaluation, and four-image Kodak sensitivity subset. The appendix testing procedures and settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The interior-gradient and flat-optimization ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, layer-ordering visualization, editability demonstration, and optimization trajectories are retained. The revised method schematics introduce no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 3 retains mean PSNR and ranges across hyperparameter settings, without changing statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, Figure 1(b), and the empirical figure findings are unchanged. For example, both report 1024-curve PSNR of 28.30 versus 26.91 for Bézier Splatting on Kodak, and 23.99 versus 23.45 on DIV2K.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical reasoning remain unchanged. The revised figures restate the existing gradient-scaling argument and curve-count/radius recurrences; they introduce no new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same hierarchical-vectorization claims, including 50× learning rates, 2.5× acceleration, and up to 1.4 dB PSNR improvement under matched curve budgets.

C2.justification: The explanations of topology collapse, structural stabilization, and the SSIM tradeoff remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the qualification that editability is local rather than a full semantic-editability solution.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same optimizer parameters, learning rates, scheduling, pruning details, pseudocode, and A100 timing information. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to differentiable rasterization, layered vectorization, and Gaussian splatting is unchanged; reference pagination merely shifts.

P1.justification: Captions for Figures 1–2 are rewritten and funding acknowledgements are added. The supplementary subtitle changes to 'Hierarchical Optimization for Fast and Stable,' while the main title retains 'Inter-Scale Orchestration.' The remaining narrative and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The central explanatory figures are substantially redesigned. Figure 1(a) becomes a three-component schematic, incorporating reworked illustrations from v1 Figure 2 and a plot of the existing radius-decay rule. Figure 2 is rebuilt as a labeled densification-and-fitting workflow. Experimental tables and visual findings are retained.

improvement.justification: The redesigned Figures 1–2 explain the component relationships and densification/fitting cycle more explicitly than v1's montage and combined overview. This provides a limited improvement in accessibility, with unchanged scientific evidence and reproducibility information. The new inconsistency between the main and supplementary titles is a small editorial drawback.
